title: "12" > 12 is an error: text is not compared with a number
query: EVALUATE ROW ( "r", IF ( "12" > 12, "Expression is true", "Expression is false" ) )

expected.error: comparison operations do not support comparing values of type Text with values of type Integer

source.quote: Other mixed data-type comparisons will return an error. For example, a formula such as ="1" > 0 returns an error stating that DAX comparison operations do not support comparing values of type Text with values of type Integer
source.supports: only Numeric with Numeric, Boolean with Boolean and String with String can be compared; anything else is an error

source.quote: =IF("12">12,"Expression is true", "Expression is false") returns "Expression is true"

derivation: The left operand is text and the right an integer. That pair is not among the supported comparisons, so the query fails.
alternative: The Power BI data types page says this very formula returns "Expression is true" (text ranks above numbers): one row, [r] = "Expression is true" (string).
notes: The Microsoft pages disagree. The operator reference says a comparison of text (or a Boolean) with a number is an error. The Power BI data types page gives a result, ranking Boolean above text and text above numbers.
